analysis: What changed versus the 8:00 AM brief: the split tape strengthened on the tech side — S&P +0.3% to +0.5%, Nasdaq +0.8% to +0.9%, Dow -0.6% to -0.2% off its lows — and the morning's two macro prints both beat: JOLTS 7.523M vs ~7.1-7.16M expected with layoffs easing, and factory orders +1.8% vs +1.2% expected. That macro support did not lift everything: Apple held near -2%, Palantir slipped back toward -3%, and Shopify stalled near -7%, while Nvidia (+3%+), Meta (+2.1%) and Microsoft (+1.7%) carried the Nasdaq leg and Tesla flipped further negative (-1.4%). Signal vs noise: the macro beats are real but backward-looking (September data); today's live catalysts are AMD after the close and overnight midterm results, with the Nvidia China-cloud report still single-source and unconfirmed. The 10-year yield easing to 4.93% from the 8:00 AM brief's 4.96% removes a small headwind for rate-sensitive groups, though homebuilders still lagged. USAC's beat gain held through its call window, the cleanest follow-through of the morning's earnings stories.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Split tape strengthened into late morning (IBD): Dow -0.2% off its lows, S&P 500 +0.5%, Nasdaq +0.9%; delayed StockSetups read: SPY +0.36%, QQQ +0.68%, DIA -0.47%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tech-led split is widening, not fading — Nasdaq strength with a still-negative Dow keeps this a rotation story, not broad risk-on.

headlines.headline: September JOLTS beat: job openings rose 333,000 to 7.523M, above 7.16M expected (Econoday via IBD) and 7.10M in the Reuters poll; August revised up to 7.19M; openings rate 4.5% (from 4.3%); hires 5.402M, layoffs 1.641M with the layoff rate down to 1.0% from 1.1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Stronger labor demand with easing layoffs — a firmer labor read that keeps the Fed-cut timing debate alive into Friday's payrolls.

headlines.headline: September factory orders beat: new orders rose 1.8% vs 1.2% expected, after an upwardly revised 0.3% August gain; orders up 7.2% year over year, led by a 28.3% jump in civilian aircraft bookings; core capital-goods orders rose 0.6%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second morning macro beat — manufacturing demand looks firmer than forecast, a mild tailwind for cyclicals even as tech dominates the tape.

headlines.headline: Apple held near -2% in late-morning trading (IBD: down more than 2%; Finnhub live: $331.21, -2.10% vs Monday's $338.32 close), after its December-quarter gross-margin guide of 45-46% (vs 47.9% in September, rising memory costs cited) outweighed fiscal Q4 EPS $2.10 vs $1.99 expected and sales $114.5B vs $113.4B expected.
headlines.why_it_matters: The margin-guide selloff is stabilizing, not reversing — holiday-quarter margin, not the September beat, still sets the price.

headlines.headline: Chips led again: Nvidia up more than 3% (IBD), Finnhub live $207.94, +2.91% vs $202.06 prior close, on pace to snap a four-day losing streak; Monolithic Power surged more than 8% and Sandisk nearly 7% among Nasdaq-100 leaders; AMD reports after the close (EPS $1.95 on $13.1B expected).
headlines.why_it_matters: The beaten-down chip group is leading the tape into AMD's print — that report decides whether this is a bounce or a reversal.

headlines.headline: Palantir slipped further to about -3% in live trading (Finnhub: $172.75, -3.13% vs $178.34 prior close; StockSetups live tape: -2.97%), after beating Q3 earnings and revenue targets as new contract value fell to $2.9B from $3.4B; on pace for a sixth straight losing session.
headlines.why_it_matters: Another beat sold on a deceleration metric — the downtrend is easing for some earnings losers, but not for Palantir yet.

headlines.headline: Shopify stayed the morning's biggest earnings loser: down more than 7% (IBD), Finnhub live $145.52, -6.85% vs $156.22 prior close, after Q3 revenue of $3.74B narrowly missed estimates — its first miss since 2022 — with subscription revenue and merchandise volume also disappointing; it fell below its 50-day moving average.
headlines.why_it_matters: The partial recovery off the ~16% premarket plunge has stalled near -7% — the size of any further bounce is the sentiment tell for the rest of the session.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split in late-morning live quotes (Finnhub): Meta $619.76, +2.15%; Microsoft $515.69, +1.69%; Amazon $248.07, +0.99%; Alphabet $278.61, -0.14%; Tesla $398.12, -1.41% versus Monday's close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Meta/Microsoft strength is carrying the Nasdaq leg while Tesla and Alphabet lag — no single megacap direction, consistent with the split index tape.

headlines.headline: Biotech broke out while software lagged: Kymera Therapeutics surged more than 4%, clearing a cup-with-handle entry of 127.85 (IBD/MarketSurge); biotech and pharma ETFs gained roughly 2% each, while Salesforce slipped 2%+ and the software ETF fell more than 1%; homebuilders fell more than 1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Sector split confirms the bounce is narrow — semis and biotech up, software and rate-sensitive homebuilders down.

headlines.headline: Carried, no update: Nvidia reportedly told cloud partners to sell at least 51% of services to non-Chinese companies under future contracts, per the Financial Times; Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied it, existing contracts are exempt, and a follow-up report said the guidance was not being enforced as a mandatory restriction.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile: if confirmed, it caps a China-demand channel for future contracts; if softened, it is noise on top of a chip bounce.

headlines.headline: Midterms today, results overnight: polls favor Democrats retaking the House, Polymarket puts Democrats at 78% for the Senate and 95% for the House (IBD); strategists cited by IBD argue a blue wave would be bad news for AI stocks.
headlines.why_it_matters: Results emerge overnight, so traders carry election risk with no scheduled announcement to trade against until polls close.

headlines.headline: Nasdaq-100 still in correction: Monday's close was more than 10% below its October 6 record, its third correction of 2026, with the semiconductor benchmark down ~12% in three sessions (carried from the 6:00 AM brief).
headlines.why_it_matters: Correction status frames every tech bounce as guilty-until-proven-innocent — AMD after the bell is the next proof point.

usac.headline: USA Compression Partners held its Q3-beat gain into late morning: MarketBeat snapshots put USAC near $25.51, +2.9% vs Monday's $24.80 close, after the 8:00 AM brief's $25.40 (+2.4%) at 10:08 AM ET; Q3 revenue $357.2M (vs $250.3M a year ago and ~$348.32M consensus), Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 in line with consensus, distribution held at $0.525. Its 11:00 AM ET (8:00 AM PT) earnings call has now wrapped; no published call takeaways were found in this hour's search.
usac.why_it_matters: The revenue beat is holding in price after a flat open — the gain survived the call window, with the $0.525 distribution paying Friday Nov 6 as the next dated item.

watch_next: Rest of the session: whether the chip bounce holds and Apple/Palantir/Shopify stabilize off early lows.
After the close today: AMD, Super Micro, Block, Amgen, Arista, Booking.
Overnight: U.S. midterm results — House favored to flip per polls, Senate uncertain.
Wed Nov 4: Treasury quarterly refunding announcement; Qualcomm and Arm after the close.
